clue.text: City thrice as loud

indicators.note: as loud asks for the word spoken out, so we want what sounds like the synonym

parts.note: thrice means three times over, triply

explanation.surface: A city where the noise is three times as great as anywhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as loud' signals a sound-alike: the capital of Libya, said quickly, sounds like 'triply'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, and also a city in Lebanon.

clue.text: Hear about one-pound hat

indicators.note: about means going round, so the court word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court
one is the Roman numeral I
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: Listen to news of a hat that costs a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like listening but is the legal sense: to try a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with an indented crown.

clue.text: Retard Philistine is deep in trouble

parts.note: Philistine is the setter of this puzzle, so 'Philistine is' becomes I'M

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of deep are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being in deep trouble, which slows things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philistine' is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter's 'is' becomes I'M; 'in trouble' rearranges the second word to make PEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to slow or hinder it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Unfit method for how to reach another phase

definitions.text: method for how to reach another phase
definitions.meaning: the word phase can be made by taking its letters out of order from the word shape

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: rearranging the letters of 'shape' gives 'phase'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfit is in poor physical condition, idiomatically out of condition.

clue.text: Not the foremost spacious room in this house

indicators.note: not the foremost tells us to drop the very first letter of the phrase

parts.note: spacious means big
loo is British slang for a toilet, a room in the house

explanation.surface: A large toilet is not the most prominent feature of this home.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British for a lavatory; 'Not the foremost' strips the B from BIGLOO.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped dwelling built from blocks of snow.

clue.text: After break I have become agitated

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the word for break

parts.note: a break is a rest
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: After a pause, I have grown restless.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive means restless and fidgety, the same as agitated.

clue.text: Music degree abandoned for the first product of French caves

indicators.note: abandoned says the degree letters are dropped from the music word

parts.note: baroque is a style of music
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
taken as written

indicators.note: the first means the opening letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Giving up a music degree in favour of a career making French cave produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music' is BAROQUE; 'abandoned' takes away BA, leaving ROQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Roquefort is a blue ewe's-milk cheese matured in the caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon in France.

clue.text: Bullet snapped

definitions.meaning: a projectile fired from a gun
photographed, as in took a picture

explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a bullet or pellet, and to have shot a picture is to have snapped it.

clue.text: One city in which I resign due to unfairness

parts.note: one is I

indicators.note: in which puts the resignation inside the city letters

parts.note: NY is New York, a city
'I resign' is 'I quit'

explanation.surface: A man quits his post because of injustice in his city.
explanation.walkthrough: NY (New York) is opened up by 'in which' to take IQUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is gross injustice or wickedness, a stronger word for unfairness.

clue.text: Lens or prosthesis back to front

indicators.note: back to front swaps the two halves so the rear word comes first

parts.note: a glass eye is an artificial eye, a prosthesis

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lens or a false eye has been fitted the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves GLASS from the front of GLASSEYE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass is a single lens such as a monocle.

clue.text: Contribution from Russian leader with part exchange

indicators.note: with part exchange says two parts of the name swap places

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is the Russian leader

explanation.surface: A Russian president contributes something in a trade-in deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with part exchange' swaps PUT and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is a contribution to a discussion or project.

clue.text: Say Scotch on the rocks is sweet

parts.note: Scotch whisky is an example of liquor, which 'say' flags
on the rocks means served with ice

explanation.surface: Whisky over ice is described as sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Scotch as one example of LIQUOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice is a black chewy confection made from a root extract, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Happy life, yet with a thorn in the side?

definitions.text: Happy life, yet with a thorn in the side?

parts.words: Happy life, yet with a thorn in the side?
parts.note: an easy, comfortable life described as a place to lie down among flowers whose stems carry prickles

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for an easy life is taken literally: lying among roses would mean thorns in your side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a situation of comfort and ease, usually used negatively.

clue.text: Source of energy, as consumed by bad case of flu

definitions.text: Source of energy, as consumed by bad case of flu

indicators.note: consumed by places the picked letter inside the jumbled letters
bad case of suggests the letters of flu are in poor shape, jumbled
source of picks out the opening letter of energy

explanation.surface: Getting energy when eaten up by a nasty dose of influenza.
explanation.walkthrough: E is put inside FUL, the letters of FLU rearranged by 'bad case of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuel is material burned to provide energy, so it is a source of power.

clue.text: Rare to include firm that's ahead of its time

indicators.note: to include places the firm inside the word for rare

parts.note: rare things are precious
CO is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An unusual company proving to be well ahead of its time.
explanation.definitionFit: Precocious describes development ahead of the usual age or time.

clue.text: Animal boxes that many swear by

parts.note: a hippo is an animal
crates are boxes

explanation.surface: Animal containers in which many people place their trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that many swear by' refers to the Hippocratic oath sworn by doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hippocratic oath, named after the Greek physician, is what new doctors swear.

clue.text: Pathetic admission of young lady who doesn't finish reading the lines

indicators.note: admission of means letting the next part in

parts.note: paltry means pathetically small

indicators.note: who doesn't finish says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: miss is a young lady

explanation.surface: A girl stops halfway through a pitiful confession while studying her script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' seems to be an actor's script, but here it means the palm's creases; 'admission of' lets the cut-short girl's title inside the word for pathetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmistry is fortune-telling by reading the lines on the palm of the hand.

clue.text: Single-minded alumni scattering seeds

parts.note: OBs are old boys, former pupils

indicators.note: scattering spreads the letters of seeds about

explanation.surface: Former pupils sowing seeds with fixed determination.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is British for a former pupil of a school; 'scattering' rearranges the sown things into SESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessed means fixated on one thing, so single-minded.

clue.text: Bits and pieces from dodgy compiler, not too smart at first

parts.note: dodgy here means odd, suspicious
the crossword setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letters of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Scraps produced by a suspect setter who was slow to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' looks like an anagram signal but gives ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover scraps and assorted remnants.

clue.text: Citizens in a state by ingesting excess drugs — and most of the police accept it

indicators.note: ingesting means taking inside

parts.note: taken as written
OD stands for overdose

indicators.note: accept, in the sense of receiving something into oneself, puts the next word inside the shortened police
most of drops the last letter

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nation's people overdosing while officers simply put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingesting' and 'accept' both signal one piece taken inside another; 'most of' drops the final E of police, and the inserted word lands after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The body politic is the people of a nation considered as one political group.

clue.text: The woman's in a tizzy, causing rupture

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of agitation, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A woman panics because she has a rupture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tizzy' jumbles IN A into NIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is a rupture in which an organ pushes through the muscle wall.

clue.text: Behind, as with rent outstanding

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: outstanding, read as standing out of place, shuffles the letters of rent

explanation.surface: Falling behind because rent has not been paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like unpaid rent but shuffles RENT into TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is a nautical term meaning behind or towards the back of a ship.

clue.text: She caused some mayhem, matchmaking

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman who stirred up chaos by setting people up romantically.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's heroine is a notorious meddling matchmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a woman's name, so it can stand for a she in a sentence.

clue.text: Those who groom pedants

definitions.meaning: people who pick lice eggs from hair, as monkeys groom
fussy people who find fault with tiny details

explanation.definitionFit: A nitpicker literally removes nits from hair and figuratively quibbles over trivia.

clue.text: Father Bear

parts.note: the word for father is pa

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as P AND A: those two letters spell PA, a father.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a black-and-white bear of China.

clue.text: Fat, lard and butter begin and end thus

definitions.text: Fat, lard and butter begin and end thus

indicators.note: begin points to the starting letters of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: Eating fats leaves you ending up with a paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: such foods end as body fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flab is soft loose body fat, the result of a fatty diet.

clue.text: Perhaps lonely heart to spill the beans twice

parts.note: to sing is to confess, to spill the beans
to let on is to reveal a secret, a second way to spill the beans

explanation.surface: A lonely-hearts advertiser confesses everything, then again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' asks for two different synonyms for confessing.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is an unattached single person, such as someone placing a lonely-hearts ad.

clue.text: Leopard attack not begun

indicators.note: not begun drops the opening letter

parts.note: to pounce is to spring and attack

explanation.surface: A big cat whose leap fails to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard.

clue.text: Pay no attention to bodies disintegrating — you may hear why

indicators.note: disintegrating breaks bodies into pieces that are reassembled
you may hear means the word is spoken, giving a letter of the same sound

parts.note: why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Ignore the decaying corpses, and you can probably hear why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disintegrating' reworks BODIES into DISOBE.
explanation.definitionFit: To disobey is to ignore an order or rule.

clue.text: Don't the upper classes leave a mark?

parts.note: A and B are the top social grades in British market research
to stain is to leave a mark

explanation.surface: Asking whether the posh never leave a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: AB refers to the British socio-economic grades A and B, the top classes.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from doing something, to choose not to.
